mechanism: Esomeprazole inhibits CYP2D6 and CYP3A4, potentially increasing oxybutynin plasma concentrations and anticholinergic effects; additive anticholinergic effects may also occur as esomeprazole has weak antimuscarinic properties.
action: Monitor for increased anticholinergic symptoms (dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, cognitive effects); consider dose adjustment of oxybutynin if needed or use alternative proton pump inhibitor with lower CYP inhibition.
